question: On 16 June 2026, Polish pilgrims from the Border Defence Movement (including Robert Bąkiewicz) who wanted to erect a cross and pray at a memorial to the Polish victims of World War II were stopped from doing so and brutally beaten by German police in Berlin. German police tolerate Muslims praying in public but attack Christian pilgrims carrying a cross.
In light of Articles 2 and 6 TEU, as well as the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights (religious freedom, non-discrimination, freedom of assembly), could the Commission answer the following questions: 1.
What is the Commission’s view on the events described above?
Will the Commission include this incident in its forthcoming report on the rule of law in the Member States?
What is the Commission's view of the selective treatment of religious gatherings by the German authorities?
